title: dss-precovery: Precovery of Known Distant Solar System Objects on Digitized Sky Survey Plates
description:
A Python tool that looks for a known, slow-moving Solar System object on the Digitized Sky Survey scans of old photographic plates (POSS-I and UK Schmidt) and measures its positions. It finds the plates taken while the object was on them, refits each plate's astrometry to Gaia DR3, searches the JPL Horizons uncertainty region, rejects stars, plate flaws and sources seen on plates from other dates (POSS-II included), and fits blended neighbors jointly.

The package includes an offline self-test, three known-answer tests (Quaoar on POSS-I plates, Quaoar and Eris on UK Schmidt plates) with their results, and D. Hill's POSS-I plate dates and clock corrections (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23549537). See README.md for installation, use and credits.
